title: Truncation tower reconstructs a quasi-coherent complex

from.place: proof, first step, truncation tower used before applying the derived functor

statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $E\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pc-derived-category]. For $n\geq0$ put $E_n=\tau_{\geq-n}E$ using the standard truncation [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category]. Then the canonical map $E\to R\varprojlim_nE_n$ is an isomorphism in $D(\mathcal O_X)$, where $R\varprojlim$ is the derived inverse limit [def-weil-derived-limit] taken in $D(\mathcal O_X)$ (the product $\prod_nE_n$ being the product in $D(\mathcal O_X)$, not in $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$; cf. Stacks Tag 08D5). If $F:\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)\to\operatorname{Ab}$ is additive, commutes with countable products, and has a right derived functor $RF$ [def-sp-left-exact-additive], then the induced map $RF(E)\to R\varprojlim_nRF(E_n)$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 08D4 (lemma-nice-K-injective, proof) and Tag 08D4 proof of part (2), first paragraph; Tags 08D3 and 08D1

proof.text: Let $\mathcal B$ be the set of affine open subschemes of $X$; it is a basis of the topology. Each cohomology sheaf $H^q(E)$ is quasi-coherent because $E\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pc-derived-category], so affine vanishing [pqf-lem-affine-vanishing] gives $H^p(U,H^q(E))=0$ for all $U\in\mathcal B$, all $p>0$ and all $q$. This is the hypothesis, with $d=0$, of the ringed-space truncation-tower lemma [lem-pc-ringed-space-truncation-derived-limit], which states that the canonical map $E\to R\varprojlim_nE_n$, $E_n=\tau_{\geq-n}E$ [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category], is an isomorphism in $D(\mathcal O_X)$, the derived limit [def-weil-derived-limit] being taken in $D(\mathcal O_X)$. (This is the proof of Stacks Tag 08D3.)

Apply the product-preserving derived-functor comparison [lem-pc-derived-functor-commutes-derived-limit] to the truncation tower (E_n), using Step 1's derived-limit identification E\simeq R\varprojlim_nE_n in D(\mathcal O_X). It gives the canonical map RF(E)\to R\varprojlim_nRF(E_n) as an isomorphism. The cited comparison is Stacks Tag 08U1 (Injectives, lemma-RF-commutes-with-Rlim), whose hypotheses are exactly additivity, countable-product preservation, and existence of the right derived functor in the present scheme/module setting (Mod(\mathcal O_X) is a Grothendieck abelian category and Ab has exact countable products; products are taken in D(\mathcal O_X) and D(\mathrm{Ab})).

The constructions are natural in E and in morphisms of towers: the truncation maps, the Roos projections, and the derived-functor comparison maps are all induced by the corresponding universal maps. Hence the two displayed isomorphisms are the canonical ones claimed in the statement.
